name: video
description: Recipe-driven HyperFrames motion graphics: same skeleton, swap the content.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for the video skills.

The authoritative mapping is not in this repo. It lives in the sibling repo `dEitY719/harness-skills` at `references/kimi-tools.md` (https://github.com/dEitY719/harness-skills/blob/main/references/kimi-tools.md) and is the single source of truth for every repo in the `dEitY719/*-skills` family; do not copy it here. Summary:

- Read / Write / Edit / Bash / Grep / Glob keep their exposed Kimi names. Every scaffold, music, lint, check, snapshot and render step in `video:hf-motion` is a plain shell command - run it with `Bash` and surface its `[OK]` / `[FAIL]` lines verbatim.
- "Ask the user" -> `AskUserQuestion`. `video:hf-motion` asks when no recipe was given and before the final render, to confirm the parameters.
- `TodoWrite` -> Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool.
- Kimi does not set `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`. Export it to this plugin's install dir before running the skill's scripts, or the skill stops at its plugin-root guard.
- Kimi has no `Skill` tool, so the engine rules the skill delegates to (`hyperframes:hyperframes-core`, `hyperframes:motion-graphics`) must be read as files from the official hyperframes plugin's `skills/` directory.

Safety contracts. These are part of the skill, not advice:

- Never render before the user has confirmed the parameters. All on-screen text comes from parameters; never invent names, numbers or claims.
- The official hyperframes plugin is a prerequisite. Invoke its CLI only through `skills/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs`, never a bare `npx hyperframes`, and never run `skills update`.
- A recipe that is listed as planned is not implemented. Say so; do not improvise it inside `intro-kinetic`.
